title: Reuse weights, select computation
subtitle: Loop scaling · Conditional interaction · Deep Double Descent
intro: One main reading and one brief: the value of loop depth depends on the budget; predicting before executing also incurs screening costs. The classic examines double descent across model size, training time, and sample count.

articles.paper: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
articles.authors: Chanakya Ekbote · Artidoro Pagnoni · Devendra Singh Sachan · Shruti Bhosale · Mike Lewis · Maryam Fazel-Zarandi · Shashank Rajput · Sujan Kumar Gonugondla
articles.title: The return to looping depends on what is held fixed
articles.evidence: Read §§2–3 and relevant Appendix G ablations; not every page of the 149-page paper; not reproduced

blocks.text: From Universal Transformer (2018) to PLT (2025), weight sharing adds effective depth, but every loop still executes. This study compares loop placement, specialization, and parallel interfaces in pretraining from scratch.[1]

blocks.label: Schematic shared transform and Loop LoRA; the latter relaxes exact sharing by loop [1]

blocks.text: Experiments span 70M–1B parameters, up to 155B tokens and 32 loops. Full-stack looping generally favors fixed parameter budgets; middle-stack looping is more competitive at fixed training FLOPs. Lower bits per byte (BPB) is better.[1]

blocks.label: Raw cross-token interface: previous-token states remove same-token serial dependence [1]

blocks.text: The repair preserves the current embedding, separately RMS-normalizes both streams, and controls their mixture. The 200M ablation uses fixed 50/50 mixing; subsequent 100M–1B experiments use a rank-8 linear gate and separate KV caches.[1]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Parameter efficiency need not imply compute efficiency; a parallel dependency graph alone does not establish end-to-end wall-clock speedup. Loop gains can saturate, reverse, or become unstable.[1]

articles.paper: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?
articles.authors: Qi Wang · Yun Qu · Lizhou Cai · Heming Zou · Haoang Chi · Yiqin Lv · Xiang Li · Haiyan Feng · Mengyu Ge · Yize Geng · Yuhang Jiang · Yixiu Mao · Xiangyang Ji
articles.title: Brief: predict value before paying execution cost
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-29 07:00 UTC (October 29 in New York) · v1
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract and related discussion in §§1 and 7.2; appendix proofs not verified

blocks.text: This Perspective proposes a lightweight predictor that screens interactions before an expensive executor acts, then updates from outcomes. Ideal savings depend on useful-interaction density; prediction errors, exploration, and drift erode them.[2]

blocks.tex: C_{\rm all}=Kc_e,\qquad C_{\rm gate}=Kc_p+\rho Kc_e,\qquad \frac{C_{\rm all}}{C_{\rm gate}}=\frac{1}{c_p/c_e+\rho}
blocks.label: Illustrative accounting: K equal-cost candidates, admitted fraction ρ, prediction/execution costs c_p/c_e; not the full paper theorem

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: This accounting assumes screening preserves the required utility; the ratio approaches 1/ρ only when prediction is negligible. The paper acknowledges that gating censors training observations, so i.i.d. error rates need not apply. Informative compute remains a testable scaling hypothesis.[2]

classic.dateNote: First posted 2019-12-05; read v1 §§2 and 4–7; ICLR 2020
classic.evidence: Read definitions, hypothesis, and experiments; linear regression below is illustrative, not a deep-network theorem from this paper

recognition.label: ICLR 2020 · important historical double-descent work (DBLP checked 2026-10-31)

classic.question: With architecture and sample size fixed, does the test-error peak still track near-zero training error when only training duration or optimizer changes?

blocks.text: Belkin et al. (2018) connected classical and interpolating regimes through double descent. This paper extends the axis from parameter count to the training procedure: one architecture can cross the critical regime as training continues.[3,4]

blocks.label: Paper definition: largest sample size fitted by procedure T with expected training error ≤ε [3]

blocks.tex: \mathrm{EMC}(\mathcal T)\ll n\ ;\quad \mathrm{EMC}(\mathcal T)\approx n\ ;\quad \mathrm{EMC}(\mathcal T)\gg n
blocks.label: Paper hypothesis: increasing effective complexity helps away from criticality but may hurt near it; not a universal theorem [3]

blocks.text: An illustrative least-squares model isolates noise amplification: X∈R^{n×p}, y=Xβ+ξ, E[ξ|X]=0, Cov(ξ|X)=σ²I; x is independent of training noise.

blocks.label: The pseudoinverse amplifies noise along small singular values; not a proof of the deep-network mechanism
Noise variance only; total prediction risk also includes bias, and the spectrum changes with data and model

rows: 15% label noise; Adam up to 4K epochs
More data hurts in a local regime

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Neither ε nor “sufficiently far” from criticality is principled in EMC. The experiments and hypothesis do not guarantee double descent for every deep network; the linear illustration does not imply decreasing risk whenever p>n.[3]
